questions.prompt: Rewriting history always does what to the affected commits?

options.text: Gives them new hashes (creates new commits)
Uploads them to the remote automatically

questions.explanation: Amend, rebase, squash, and bulk tools all produce new commits with new hashes. That's precisely why rewriting shared history is disruptive.

questions.prompt: Which force-push is safer, and why?

options.text: --force-with-lease, because it aborts if the remote has commits you haven't seen

questions.explanation: --force-with-lease refuses the push if the remote advanced unexpectedly, protecting a teammate's commits from being clobbered — unlike unconditional --force.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: amend, rebase, and squash all rewrite history
git filter-repo is recommended over git filter-branch for bulk rewrites
You should only rewrite history that hasn't been shared, unless you coordinate
Removing a leaked secret from history means you no longer need to rotate it

questions.explanation: Those rewrite commits, filter-repo is the recommended bulk tool, and unshared-only is the safe rule. A leaked secret must still be rotated — the rewrite can't recall existing copies.

questions.prompt: The safer force-push that refuses if the remote moved unexpectedly is: git push --force-with-______
questions.explanation: git push --force-with-lease checks that the remote ref is where you last saw it before overwriting, avoiding clobbering unseen commits.

questions.prompt: You purged a leaked API key from all history and force-pushed. Is the key safe now?

options.text: No — treat it as compromised and rotate it, since copies may persist in clones, forks, and caches
Yes, as long as the repo is private
Only if you also deleted the branch

questions.explanation: History rewriting reduces future exposure but can't recall copies that already exist. The leaked key must be rotated (revoked and replaced) to be safe.

questions.prompt: Match each tool to its scope.

pairs.right: Rewrite a range of recent commits
Rewrite the entire history in bulk

questions.explanation: amend touches the last commit, rebase -i a range, filter-repo all of history, and --force-with-lease updates a rewritten branch safely.
